analysis.title: What's next for European bonds and the euro after Lagarde's resignation?
key_insights: The ECB held rates unchanged as expected but said risks to inflation remain tilted to higher readings as oil and gas prices keep rising. It said underlying inflation is broadly stable and wages have not responded materially to higher prices.

The ECB decision came hours after President Christine Lagarde announced she will leave office early on 7 February 2027. UBS expects a smooth transition and policy continuity, with the near-term path driven by inflation, wages, growth and financing conditions rather than the leadership change.

The ECB has raised rates twice this year. Inflation is running at roughly twice the 2% target, which keeps a December hike in play, though policymakers are not in a hurry without clearer evidence of persistent inflation or second-round effects.

UBS expects Eurozone sovereign yields to decline into next year despite volatile French spreads. It does not think energy and inflation developments justify the market's pricing of an additional 75bps of ECB tightening.

If spread pressure is judged unjustified and disruptive to policy transmission, the ECB's first line of defence would probably be flexible reinvestment of maturing bond holdings, with the never-used Transmission Protection Instrument available beyond that.

UBS favors short- to medium-term European bonds (select agency, covered and corporate) and stronger investment grade issuers at medium maturities. It is cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal concerns and heavy issuance.

UBS expects EURUSD to recover toward 1.16 by year-end, arguing the decline has exceeded what fundamentals imply. It advises investors to progressively reduce excess US dollar holdings where appropriate.

The Fed held at 3.75-4% on 28 October. The statement upgraded growth to 'strong' from 'solid' and two policymakers preferred a 25-basis-point hike. Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference was more balanced, citing improving inflation expectations and tighter financial and credit conditions.

The Nasdaq fell 1.4% on Thursday. Alphabet dropped 12.3% after most core businesses reported September-quarter sales below expectations. Amazon fell 7.3% after hours on its slowest e-commerce growth in three years and capex above forecasts.

Cloud growth accelerated across hyperscalers: Google Cloud revenue +103% y/y, Microsoft Azure +48%, Oracle cloud +62%, and Amazon's cloud unit accelerated for a sixth straight quarter. Microsoft reported an eight-fold increase in large Copilot accounts and Alphabet said Gemini reached 1 billion users.

UBS forecasts aggregate AI capex of USD 1tr in 2026, USD 1.4tr in 2027 and USD 1.5tr in 2028. It favors well-funded hyperscalers and quality semiconductor and hardware names and is cautious on specialized AI cloud providers.

September PCE price index rose 0.5% m/m (largest since March) to 3.6% y/y. Core PCE rose 0.3% m/m and 3.1% y/y, in line with consensus. 3Q GDP grew at a 3.4% annualized rate versus a 3.1% estimate and 2.2% in 2Q.

UBS expects the Fed to hike 25bps in December and again in March, and does not think a moderate tightening cycle will derail the US economy or equity rally. It suggests using elevated yields to add selectively to medium- and longer-duration high-quality bonds.

Shares fell 7.3% after hours on the slowest e-commerce growth in three years and capex above forecasts, while the cloud unit accelerated for a sixth consecutive quarter.

sector_views.rationale: Accelerating cloud revenue and AI adoption suggest infrastructure spending is turning into revenue. UBS favors well-funded hyperscalers and quality semiconductor and hardware names, is cautious on specialized AI cloud providers, and advises concentrated holders to diversify.

French fiscal and political risks widen sovereign spreads without credible fiscal consolidation.
Heavy issuance and fiscal concerns keep volatility elevated at the longest maturities.

Tighter financing conditions weigh on growth.

French fiscal and political risks are keeping sovereign spreads volatile.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects European yields to decline into next year because energy and inflation developments are unlikely to justify the additional 75bps of ECB tightening priced by the market, so duration is well compensated.
tension_points.bear_case: The energy shock could prove persistent and generate second-round effects. Inflation is around twice the 2% target and a December hike is in play. French spreads could widen further without credible fiscal consolidation.
tension_points.what_invalidates: More persistent inflation or second-round effects from the energy shock, which the ECB said could require further tightening.

tension_points.bull_case: Cloud revenue accelerated across hyperscalers (Google Cloud +103%, Azure +48%, Oracle +62%) and Copilot and Gemini adoption is rising, supporting the capex forecast of USD 1.4tr in 2027.
tension_points.bear_case: Elevated expectations and company-specific misses (Alphabet -12.3%, Amazon -7.3% after hours on capex above forecasts) are likely to drive continued volatility.
